title: The Wall Between Our Gardens
eyebrow: a slow autumn day · garden to table
lesson: Kindness doesn't always need words; sometimes it is just something left on the wall.

places.garden: her small kitchen garden behind a grey stone cottage in the Lake District hills in late autumn: four low raised wooden beds (kale, leeks, the last orange pumpkins on browning vines, a clump of sage), a wet gravel path, a small old apple tree with a few red apples left, and at the far side a waist-high mossy dry-stone wall dividing her garden from her elderly neighbour's; over the wall his small white cottage with a slate roof and a chimney with a thin line of smoke; green fells softened by mist behind
places.kitchen: her small cottage kitchen: whitewashed stone walls, a pale scrubbed wood worktop, a white butler sink under a small-paned window that looks onto the garden and the stone wall, a sage-green two-ring cooker with one heavy cream enamel pot, a small round pale wood table by the window with two plain chairs, a few herbs in clay pots on the sill

light.morning: Early morning, soft cool daylight, light mist lifting off the garden.
light.late morning: Late morning, bright soft overcast daylight.
light.noon rain: Midday, bright grey daylight; soft rain falling outside.
light.afternoon: Afternoon, the rain has stopped and soft sun breaks through, wet leaves shining.
light.dusk: Dusk, soft blue fading daylight outside and one plain warm lamp on inside; everything clearly visible.
light.next morning: The next morning, soft bright daylight, a little mist.

outfits.day: an oatmeal chunky-knit cardigan over a long moss-green corduroy pinafore dress, dark-green rubber boots in the garden
outfits.cooking: an oatmeal chunky-knit cardigan with the sleeves pushed to the forearm over a long moss-green corduroy pinafore dress, a faded mustard linen apron
outfits.dusk: an oatmeal chunky-knit cardigan, a long moss-green corduroy pinafore dress, a cream wool scarf, dark-green rubber boots
outfits.next morning: a soft rust-brown crew-neck jumper and loose navy cotton trousers

garden.brief: The garden empty, nobody in it, seen from the back door of the cottage: the raised beds, the gravel path, the apple tree and the mossy dry-stone wall at the far side with the neighbour's white cottage and smoking chimney beyond. Bright soft overcast daylight.

kitchen.brief: The kitchen empty, nobody in it, seen from the doorway: the butler sink under the small-paned window onto the garden, the worktop, the sage-green cooker with the cream enamel pot, the small round table. Bright soft daylight.

Pip.brief: Pip the cat sitting upright on the wet gravel path of the garden, looking slightly to the side, full body in view, bright soft overcast daylight.

the wicker trug.brief: A shallow oval wicker garden trug basket with a curved wooden handle, empty, standing on a pale wood worktop, bright soft daylight, plain background.

beats.vo: Every week, something shows up on the wall between my garden and Mr. Hale's. And he's never once mentioned it.
beats.shot: Close-up on top of the mossy dry-stone wall: three brown hen's eggs resting in the moss, droplets of mist on the stones; her hand in an oatmeal knit sleeve has just closed gently around the first egg.
beats.move: Her hand slowly lifts the first egg from the moss with a soft scrape of shell on stone and draws it out of frame; the other two eggs stay where they are.

beats.shot: Wide view of the whole garden in the early morning mist: the raised beds, the apple tree, the mossy wall, the neighbour's white cottage beyond with a thin line of smoke from its chimney, the fells pale in the mist.

beats.vo: Last week it was honey. Before that, a bag of plums. This morning, three eggs. Still warm.
beats.shot: Ellie seen from behind and a little to the side, walking slowly along the wet gravel path toward the cottage, the three brown eggs cupped in both hands against her cardigan.
beats.move: She walks two slow steps along the path with the soft crunch of boots on wet gravel and stops; the camera stays locked off, it does not follow her.

beats.shot: Close-up of the kitchen windowsill: a small blue-and-white enamel bowl holding the three uneven brown eggs, a clay pot of thyme beside it, the misty garden soft through the small-paned window.

beats.vo: He's eighty-one. He says morning, and that's about it. So I've never really known how to say thank you.
beats.shot: Ellie seen from the side at the small round table by the window, head bowed, eyes on a plain white mug she holds in both hands, steam rising from the tea, the misty garden and the stone wall outside the window.
beats.move: Steam curls slowly up from the mug; she lifts it a little and breathes in, then lowers it; nothing else moves.

beats.vo: So today I'm going to cook him lunch. From the garden. Wish me luck.
beats.shot: Top-down close-up of the pale wood table: her hands in oatmeal knit sleeves hold a pencil over a small open notebook with a few short handwritten lines too small and soft to read, the white mug of tea beside it.
beats.move: Her hand slowly writes one more short line with the soft scratch of pencil on paper, then taps the pencil once on the page.

beats.shot: Close-up in the raised bed: a small round deep-orange pumpkin on a browning vine among big frost-edged leaves; her two hands in oatmeal knit sleeves hold it.
beats.move: Her hands slowly twist the pumpkin until the dry stem breaks with a soft woody snap and she lifts it out of the leaves.

beats.vo: Pumpkin. A couple of leeks. A bit of sage. That's the plan.
beats.shot: Close-up of a raised bed of leeks: her hand in an oatmeal knit sleeve grips one leek low at the soil.
beats.move: Her hand slowly pulls the leek up out of the dark wet soil with a soft tearing sound of roots; a little soil falls from the white roots.

beats.shot: The wicker trug on the gravel path by the raised bed, holding the small orange pumpkin, two long leeks with soil on their roots and a bunch of soft grey-green sage.

beats.vo: Pip has other plans. Pip has decided the basket is a bed.
beats.shot: Pip the cat curled up asleep inside the wicker trug on the gravel path, lying on top of the two leeks, the small orange pumpkin beside him, bright soft overcast daylight.
beats.move: Pip slowly stretches one white front paw over the edge of the basket, flexes it, and settles again with a small sigh; the basket stays still.

beats.vo: We negotiated. He kept the basket.
beats.shot: Close-up: her hand in an oatmeal knit sleeve gently strokes Pip's grey head as he lies curled in the wicker trug on the leeks, his eyes half closed.
beats.move: Her hand strokes his head slowly once, back to front; Pip closes his eyes and pushes his head into her hand with a soft purr.

beats.vo: And a few apples. Because I can't cook for someone without making pudding. My gran would never forgive me.
beats.shot: Ellie seen from the side under the small apple tree, reaching up with one hand to a red apple on a low branch, the other hand holding the hem of her apron.
beats.move: She slowly twists the apple off the branch with a soft snap of the stalk and lowers it into her apron; the leaves move a little in the breeze.

beats.shot: A robin standing on top of the mossy dry-stone wall, the neighbour's white cottage soft behind it, bright soft overcast daylight.
beats.move: The robin hops once along the wall, tilts its head, and sings a short soft phrase.

beats.shot: Close-up at the white butler sink: water running from the tap over two long leeks held in her hands in mustard apron and pushed-up oatmeal sleeves, soil washing off the white roots, rain on the window behind.
beats.move: Water runs over the leeks with a steady soft splash; her fingers slowly rub the soil from the roots.

beats.vo: I don't really use recipes. Butter, leeks, and you wait until the kitchen smells good.
beats.shot: Close-up into the cream enamel pot on the cooker: a knob of butter melting among pale green sliced leeks, a wooden spoon resting against the rim.
beats.move: The butter bubbles and sizzles softly around the leeks and a little steam rises; nothing else moves.

beats.shot: Close-up: her hand in a pushed-up oatmeal sleeve tips a wooden board of already-cut deep-orange pumpkin cubes into the cream enamel pot of soft green leeks.
beats.move: The orange pumpkin cubes slide off the board into the pot with a soft tumble and a hiss of butter; steam rises.

beats.vo: Then it started to rain. Of course it did.
beats.shot: Close-up of the small-paned kitchen window: rain running down the glass, the garden and the stone wall blurred and green outside, a clay pot of thyme on the sill.
beats.move: Raindrops run slowly down the glass with the soft patter of rain; the room stays perfectly still.

beats.shot: Pip the cat sitting on the inside windowsill beside the thyme pot, seen from the side, watching the rain run down the glass, bright grey daylight.
beats.move: Pip's head follows one raindrop slowly down the glass, his ears twitch once; the tip of his tail moves.

beats.vo: Too much salt? Maybe. No. It's fine. It's soup.
beats.shot: Ellie seen from the side at the cooker, head bowed, eyes on a wooden spoon of smooth bright-orange pumpkin soup she holds near her lips, the cream enamel pot of orange soup steaming in front of her.
beats.move: She blows softly on the spoon, tastes, pauses with her eyes on the pot, and tilts her head a little, thinking; steam rises from the pot.

beats.shot: Close-up on the worktop: her hands in pushed-up oatmeal sleeves pour smooth bright-orange pumpkin soup from a small cream jug into a tall clear glass clip-top jar that is already half full of the same orange soup.
beats.move: A slow steady ribbon of orange soup pours into the jar with a soft glug; steam rises from the open top.

beats.shot: Top-down close-up: her two hands in pushed-up oatmeal sleeves rubbing cold butter into flour and brown sugar in a wide cream ceramic bowl, rough crumbs forming between her fingertips.
beats.move: Her fingertips slowly rub the butter and flour together and let the crumbs fall back into the bowl with a soft dry patter.

beats.vo: Crumble is the most forgiving pudding there is. Honestly, you can't get it wrong.
beats.shot: Close-up of a small oval white baking dish full of already-sliced red-skinned apples; her hand in a pushed-up oatmeal sleeve scatters a handful of rough golden crumble over them.
beats.move: The crumble falls from her fingers onto the apples in a soft light patter; nothing else moves.

beats.shot: The small table by the window: a white mug of tea with a little steam and an open paperback face down beside it, the wet garden shining in soft sun through the small-paned window, drops still on the glass.

beats.vo: Okay. You can get it a little wrong. One side is sort of dark.
beats.shot: Close-up: her two hands in a padded cream oven glove set the small oval white baking dish of apple crumble on a wooden board; the golden crumble is a little lopsided and one end of it is clearly burnt dark brown, apple juice bubbling at the edge.
beats.move: She sets the dish down with a soft clunk and lets go; the apple juice bubbles quietly at the edge and a little steam rises.

beats.vo: So the good side faces out. That's called presentation.
beats.shot: Close-up on the wooden board: the small oval white baking dish of apple crumble with one end burnt dark brown; her hand in an oven glove rests on the dish.
beats.move: Her gloved hand slowly turns the dish half a turn on the board with a soft scrape, so the burnt end faces away and the golden side faces the camera.

beats.shot: Close-up of big frost-edged kale leaves in the raised bed after the rain, full of round water droplets, soft sun breaking through.
beats.move: A water drop slowly runs down a kale leaf and falls; the leaves tremble a little in the breeze.

beats.shot: Close-up on the worktop: the wicker trug holding the tall glass clip-top jar full of bright-orange pumpkin soup and the small oval white dish of apple crumble; her hands in oatmeal knit sleeves fold a blue-and-white checked tea towel over the dish.
beats.move: Her hands slowly tuck the tea towel in around the dish; the jar stays where it is.

beats.vo: I didn't knock. That felt like too much. I just did what he does.
beats.shot: Ellie seen from behind on the wet gravel path at dusk, carrying the wicker trug with the covered dish and the jar of orange soup toward the mossy stone wall, the neighbour's window lit warm beyond it.
beats.move: She walks two slow steps toward the wall with the soft crunch of gravel and stops; the camera stays locked off, it does not follow her.

beats.shot: Close-up on top of the mossy dry-stone wall at dusk: her two hands in oatmeal knit sleeves set down the wicker trug holding the jar of orange soup and the dish under the checked tea towel, the neighbour's lit window soft beyond.
beats.move: Her hands set the basket down on the moss with a soft creak of wicker, rest a moment, and slowly withdraw.

beats.vo: And then I spent an hour pretending I wasn't looking out of the window.
beats.shot: Ellie seen from the side at the butler sink at dusk, washing the cream enamel pot under the tap, her eyes lifted to the dark-blue window where the neighbour's lit window glows small across the garden.
beats.move: Her hands slowly turn the pot under the running water while her eyes stay on the window; water runs softly.

beats.vo: In the morning, the basket was back. Jar washed. Dish washed. And a note.
beats.shot: Close-up on top of the mossy dry-stone wall in the morning: the wicker trug holding the empty clean glass jar and the clean empty white dish, a small folded piece of paper tucked under the jar; her hand in a rust-brown jumper sleeve reaches for the paper.
beats.move: Her fingers slowly slide the folded note out from under the jar with a soft rustle of paper.

beats.vo: It said, bit salty. Same time next week?
beats.shot: Ellie seen from the side at the small round table by the window, in a rust-brown jumper, head bowed, eyes on a small unfolded note in her hands, the handwriting too small to read, morning light.
beats.move: She reads, pauses, and a small quiet smile slowly comes to her face; she lowers the note to the table.

beats.vo: So now there are two of us leaving things on the wall. Nobody says much. I think that's the point.
beats.shot: Close-up of the small note on the pale wood table in morning light, folded open, the soft pencil handwriting too small and blurred to read, the blue-and-white enamel bowl of eggs beside it.

beats.vo: Next week. Less salt.
beats.shot: Wide view of the garden in the morning sun with light mist: Pip the cat sitting on top of the mossy dry-stone wall, the neighbour's white cottage behind with a thin line of smoke rising from its chimney.
beats.move: Pip slowly washes one white paw; the chimney smoke drifts up softly; the mist moves a little over the fells.
